unit.title: Ограничения мобильных игр: батарея, память и жизненный цикл

learning_outcomes.statement: Covers battery, thermal throttling, memory pressure and OS-driven app lifecycle, then answers honestly whether a Pygame project can be published to the App Store and Google Play.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Covers battery, thermal throttling, memory pressure and OS-driven app lifecycle, then answers honestly whether a Pygame project can be published to the App Store and Google Play.

Sustained CPU/GPU load drains battery and can trigger thermal throttling -- a system-imposed clock reduction that makes the game stutter for reasons unrelated to code quality. -- Confirmed -- accurate description, correctly glossed in Russian.
Neither pygame nor pygame-ce has an official 'build an APK / build for iOS' command. -- Confirmed -- no such command exists; packaging is entirely third-party.

python-for-android's main repository has no accepted official pygame-ce recipe -- only open community pull requests and user recipes. -- Confirmed -- the kivy/python-for-android recipe listing contains no pygame/pygame-ce recipe directory, and PR #2971 ('Pygame-ce on Android') is open and unmerged.

The iOS route is a community tool whose own author calls it undertested, not production-ready, and has not personally tested App Store builds. -- Confirmed almost verbatim -- seekerluke/pygame-ios README: 'This library is not well tested, and shouldn't be considered production ready'; 'Most importantly, I haven't tested App Store builds yet'.
